title: Grade 3 Math — Tue, Jun 24
description: Fractions — Day 2 of 5: Unit fractions — shading and identifying
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What is a unit fraction?
options: A fraction where both numbers are equal
A fraction with 1 as the numerator
A fraction greater than 1
A fraction with numerator bigger than denominator
questions.explanation: A unit fraction has 1 as the numerator. Examples: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5. They represent one equal part of a whole.

questions.question: Which of these is a unit fraction?
questions.explanation: 1/8 is a unit fraction because the numerator is 1. The others (3/4, 2/5, 4/4) have numerators greater than 1.

questions.question: A rectangle is divided into 5 equal parts. One part is shaded. Which unit fraction is shown?
questions.explanation: 1 part shaded out of 5 equal parts = 1/5 (one-fifth). This is a unit fraction.

questions.question: Which unit fraction is the LARGEST?
questions.explanation: 1/2 is the largest unit fraction here. When comparing unit fractions, the smaller the denominator, the larger the fraction. 1/2 > 1/5 > 1/8 > 1/10.

questions.question: How many equal parts must a whole be divided into if you want to shade 1/4 of it?
questions.explanation: The denominator 4 tells us the whole is divided into 4 equal parts. You shade 1 of those 4 parts to get 1/4.

questions.question: Which unit fraction is the SMALLEST?
questions.explanation: 1/9 is the smallest. With unit fractions, a bigger denominator means a smaller fraction because the whole is divided into more parts. 1/9 < 1/6 < 1/3 < 1/2.

questions.question: If you eat 1/4 of a cake and your sister eats 1/2 of the same cake, who ate more?
options: Your sister (1/2)
Both ate the same
Cannot compare
questions.explanation: 1/2 means half the cake; 1/4 means a quarter. Half is bigger than a quarter. Your sister ate more.

questions.question: Arrange in increasing order (smallest to largest): 1/5, 1/3, 1/8
questions.explanation: For unit fractions, bigger denominator = smaller fraction. So: 1/8 < 1/5 < 1/3. Increasing order: 1/8, 1/5, 1/3.

questions.question: A whole watermelon is 1. You cut it into 6 equal slices. One slice = what fraction?
questions.explanation: 1 slice out of 6 equal slices = 1/6 (one-sixth). This is a unit fraction.

questions.question: 4 unit fractions: 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8. What pattern do you notice in their denominators?
options: Denominators go up by 1
Denominators are consecutive even numbers, doubling the division each time
Denominators are all odd
There is no pattern
questions.explanation: 2, 4, 6, 8 are consecutive even numbers. Each one divides the whole into more equal parts: halves, quarters, sixths, eighths.

questions.question: A string is 1 metre long. If 1/5 of it is cut off, how many equal pieces was it divided into?
questions.explanation: The denominator 5 tells us the string was divided into 5 equal pieces. 1/5 means 1 of those 5 pieces was cut.

questions.question: Why does a bigger denominator make a unit fraction SMALLER?
options: Because bigger numbers are always smaller fractions
The whole is divided into more equal parts, so each individual part is smaller
Because the numerator gets bigger too
It doesn't — bigger denominators make bigger fractions
questions.explanation: Think of 1/2 vs 1/10: if you divide a pizza into 2 pieces, each piece is big (1/2). If you divide it into 10 pieces, each piece is tiny (1/10). More divisions = smaller each piece.

questions.question: Which number line correctly places 1/2 and 1/4? (0 is left, 1 is right)
options: 1/4 is at the middle; 1/2 is to its right
1/2 is at the middle; 1/4 is to its left
Both are at the same position
1/2 is to the left of 1/4
questions.explanation: 1/2 is exactly in the middle of 0 and 1. 1/4 is at the quarter-mark, which is to the LEFT of 1/2 (smaller). So 1/4 is left of 1/2.

questions.question: If 1/7 of a bag of sweets = 3 sweets, how many sweets are in the whole bag?
questions.explanation: 1/7 = 3 sweets means the bag is divided into 7 equal groups of 3. Total = 7 × 3 = 21 sweets.

questions.question: Leena has 1/3 of her homework done. Sonu has 1/4 done. Who has MORE homework remaining?
options: Leena
Sonu
Both have the same amount remaining
Cannot tell
questions.explanation: Leena done: 1/3 → remaining: 2/3. Sonu done: 1/4 → remaining: 3/4. Since 3/4 > 2/3, Sonu has more remaining.
